title: Eye Irritation Test (EIT) for Hazard Identification of Eye Irritating Chemicals using Reconstructed Human Cornea-like Epithelial (RhCE) Tissue Model
protocol: Upon receipt of the RhCE kit, check all components for integrity.
Equilibrate tissues in their 24-well shipping container to room temperature for 15 min.
Under sterile conditions, open the plastic bag containing the 24-well plate with the RhCE tissues and remove the sterile gauze.
Inspect all tissues for air bubbles between the agarose gel and insert.
Label the 6-well plates with the test article or control codes and exposure times.
Aliquot 1.0 ml of Assay Medium, pre-warmed to approximately 37 °C, into the wells of pre-labeled 6-well plates.
Use sterile forceps to remove each insert containing the RhCE tissue and place the insert in the labeled 6-well plate.
Remove any remaining shipping agarose that adheres to the outer sides of the insert by gentle blotting on sterile filter paper.
Release any air bubbles trapped underneath the inserts.
Pre-incubate the RhCE tissues in the 6-well plates to standard culture conditions (SCC, humidified atmosphere with 5 ± 1% CO2 at 37 ± 1 °C) for 1 hr.
After 1 hour, replace the Assay Medium with 1.0 ml of fresh prewarmed Assay Medium at 37°C.
Incubate RhCE tissues overnight (16-24 hours) under specified conditions.
Apply 20 µl of Ca2+ Mg2+-free-Dulbecco’s Phosphate Buffered Saline (DPBS).
Gently tap the insert on the plate to ensure DPBS wets the entire tissue surface.
Incubate RhCE tissues for 30 ± 2 minutes under specified conditions.
Topically apply 50 µl of liquid test articles using a pipette.
Expose liquids for 30 minutes.
Apply 50 mg of solid test articles using a leveled spoonful calibrated to hold 50 mg of sodium chloride.
Expose solids for 6 hours.
Place vials with test articles in a water bath at 37 °C for 15 min if necessary.
Follow EIT protocol for liquids for test articles that liquefy at 37 °C.
Use a positive displacement pipette for particularly viscous materials.
Dose the negative control and positive controls first.
Apply 50 µl of the negative control to RhCE tissues using a standard pipette.
The negative control is sterile de-ionized water.
Apply 50 µl of the positive control to RhCE tissues using a standard pipette.
The positive control is methyl acetate (CAS# 79-20-9).
Apply NC and PC for 30 min when testing liquid test articles.
Apply NC and PC for 6 hr when testing solid test articles.
Dose test articles after the negative and positive controls.
Leave a 1 min interval between applications of each test article.
Topically apply 50 µl of NC, PC, and each liquid test article to RhCE tissues using an appropriate pipetting device.
Apply 50 μl of the liquid test article directly onto the tissue to cover the upper surface.
Cut off the narrow point of the pipette tip to widen the orifice for viscous materials.
For very viscous materials, apply the test article to a dosing device.
Invert the dosing device and place it onto the tissue so that the test article evenly contacts the tissue surface.
If test article does not spread across the tissue, gently tap the insert.
Incubate the tissues at SCC for 30 ± 2 min.
Leave 2 min intervals between applications of each test article to ensure equal exposure for all tissues.
After the 30 ± 2 min DPBS pre-treatment, apply 50 μl of NC and PC topically on the RhCE tissues using an appropriate pipetting device.
For solid test article application, remove the inserts (n = 2) from the well and place them onto a sterile surface.
Topically apply approximately 50 mg of the test article onto the tissue surface using a leveled spoon.
Ensure the entire tissue surface is completely covered by the test article.
If necessary, shake the insert gently from side to side to ensure full coverage without damaging the tissue.
Grind crystalline powders with a mortar and pestle for better contact between the test article and the tissue.
Alternatively, use a 1 ml syringe with its head cut off to place powders directly onto the tissue culture inside the insert.
Stuff powders into the syringe when the plunger is drawn back and then apply by pressing the plunger down.
Wipe any contaminants from the outer wall of the insert with a sterile gauze if needed.
Incubate the tissues in 6-well plates containing culture medium at SCC for 6 h ± 15 min after dosing.
Prepare three clean beakers (150 ml capacity) per test article and fill each with 100 ml of DPBS.
Utilize a different set of three beakers for each test article.
Remove and discard the dosing device if used at the end of the exposure period.
Lift the inserts containing RhCE tissue by grasping the upper edge of the plastic collar with fine forceps.
Rinse the tissues two at a time in DPBS, holding duplicate inserts together using forceps.
Dip the inserts into the first beaker of DPBS and swirl for approximately 2 seconds.
Lift the inserts so that they are mostly filled with DPBS and decant the liquid back into the beaker.
Repeat this process three times in the first beaker.
Rinse the inserts in the second and third beakers of DPBS three times each, following the same procedure as before.
Decant any remaining liquid onto an absorbent material.
Rotate the insert to a 45° angle with the open end down and touch the upper lip to the absorbent material.
Immerse tissues in 5 ml of pre-warmed Assay Medium in a labeled 12-well plate immediately after rinsing.
Incubate liquid materials for 12 ± 2 minutes at room temperature.
Incubate solid materials for 25 ± 2 minutes at room temperature.
Decant the Assay Medium from the tissues and blot the inserts onto an absorbent material.
Transfer the inserts into the pre-labeled 6-well plate containing 1 ml of warm Assay Medium.
Incubate the tissues for 120 ± 15 min at SCC for liquid test materials.
Incubate the tissues for 18 ± 0.25 hr at SCC for solid test materials.
Prepare a commercial MTT kit according to Table 5.
Thaw the MTT concentrate at room temperature for 2 hours before use.
Combine 2 ml of the MTT concentrate with 8 ml of the MTT diluent to produce a 1.0 mg/ml MTT solution.
Store the MTT solution at 4 °C in the dark until use, do not store more than one day.
Remove each insert from the 6-well plate and gently blot on an absorbent material after Post-Incubation period.
Place the inserts into a pre-labeled 24-well plate containing 0.3 ml of MTT solution.
Release any air bubbles trapped underneath the inserts.
Incubate the plate for 180 ± 10 min at SCC.
Incubate samples in MTT solution for 180 ± 10 minutes.
Remove inserts from the 24-well plate and blot the bottom on absorbent material.
Transfer inserts into a pre-labeled 24-well plate containing 2.0 ml isopropanol for submerged extraction of non-colorant liquid test articles.
For solids and liquid colorants, transfer inserts into a pre-labeled 6-well plate with 1.0 ml isopropanol for non-submerged extraction.
Seal the plates using parafilm or a standard plate sealer.
Shake the sealed plates on an orbital shaker for 2 to 3 hours at room temperature.
Alternatively, perform overnight extraction at 2-8 °C in the dark without shaking.
At the end of the extraction period, decant liquid from each insert back into the well and discard inserts with RhCE tissues.
Mix the extract solution thoroughly.
Transfer two 200 µl aliquots of the extract into appropriate wells of a pre-labeled 96-well plate.
Discard tissues at the end of the extraction period without piercing them.
Add 1.0 ml of extractant solution to each well in a 24-well plate containing tissue extracts.
Mix the extractant solution thoroughly.
Transfer two 200 µl aliquots from each well into appropriate wells of a pre-labeled 96-well plate according to the configuration.
Centrifuge turbid extract solutions at 4 °C prior to measuring optical density if necessary.
Measure the optical density (OD) of extracted samples at a wavelength between 550 and 590 nm using a plate reader or spectrophotometer.
Subtract OD Blk from each OD value of the same experiment.
Calculate the mean value of the two aliquots for each tissue (= corrected OD).
Calculate the percent viability of each of the two replicate tissues for each control and test article relative to the average negative control (100% control).
Calculate the difference of the viability between two replicate tissues.
Calculate the mean test article viability (TA viability) and classify the test article according to the prediction model.
If the TA-treated tissue viability is >60.0 relative to NC-treated tissue viability, label the test article as non-irritant (NI).
If the TA-treated tissue viability is ≤ 60.0 relative to NC-treated tissue viability, label the test article as irritant (I).
